sense: far away, out of the way

terms.gloss: remote, out of the way, secluded
evidence: Caes. BG 7.1: silvestribus ac remōtīs locīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The participle of removeō: moved away, so far off and private; with ā, away from (cīvitās ā cōnspectū remōta, Cic. Verr. 2.3.85).

evidence: Cic. Imp. Pomp. 47: ex locīs tam longinquīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Distant in space, and in time long-lasting; from far away is ex longinquō (see far).

phrases.latin: ut quis ex longinquō revēnerat, mīrācula narrābant, vim turbinum et inaudītās volucrīs, mōnstra maris, ambiguās hominum et bēluārum fōrmās, vīsa sīve ex metū crēdita
phrases.english: whoever came back from far away told of marvels: violent whirlwinds and unheard-of birds, sea monsters, shapes half human and half beast, things seen or believed out of fear

phrases.latin: Per tēlescopium videntur remōta ut proxima.
phrases.english: Through a telescope remote things look close at hand.

sources: Lewis & Short: removeo · Lewis & Short: longinquus
